sources.figmaCaveat: The library publishes 53 scheme names and descriptions, no hex values. Every colour here is DERIVED from each scheme's documented hue/chroma/temperature and then contrast-verified; the figma.scheme number travels with each palette for auditing.
sources.contrastStandard: WCAG 2.1 AA — 4.5:1 text, 3:1 large text and UI components.

minimal.name: Minimal
minimal.blurb: Opaque surfaces. Fastest to render and the most legible under heavy density.

acrylic.name: Acrylic
acrylic.blurb: Windows Fluent acrylic. A single soft blur behind overlays and navigation.

liquid-glass.name: Liquid Glass
liquid-glass.blurb: Apple-style layered glass. Lens edges, a lit top edge and a sheen.

figma.name: Inked
figma.note: Teal accent on pure grayscale — the article calls the accent an affordance colour, not a mood colour.

figma.name: Wraith
figma.note: Dark warm-brown ground with one emerald accent; grays and white 'create a sense of balance'.

figma.name: Lapis velvet evening
figma.note: Deep blue + plum; 'the most forgiving base for long reading sessions and dense figures' per the shortlist.

figma.name: Yacht club
figma.note: Indigo on cool gray with a warm mahogany secondary — 'deeper shades add a grounding quality'.

figma.name: Amber walnut morning
figma.note: Single warm-brown family with 'excellent contrast' — no colour noise in a 200-row table.

figma.name: Honey opal sunset
figma.note: Mustard + taupe, one warm earth axis; yellow is the natural attention accent.

figma.name: Rose quartz evening
figma.note: Maroon ground reads 'serious and financial rather than playful'; blush tint for row banding.

figma.name: Cocoa topaz noonday
figma.note: Brown ground + one bright orange focal — the article names buttons/headlines as its use.

figma.name: Amethyst mint harmony
figma.note: Moody purple/emerald base; the article mandates using its four bold hues 'sparingly'.

figma.name: Royal glimmer
figma.note: Deep jewel tones — ruby accent on a near-neutral jewel ground.

figma.name: Ink wash
figma.note: Monochromatic gray — 'ideal for websites and apps that prioritize readability'; colour never does layout work.

figma.name: Frosted aura
figma.note: Slate gray + darker blue + pewter on stark white — named for law firms and financial institutions.

figma.name: Slate
figma.note: The only scheme naming fintech directly: pastel green accent on neutral gray, for status chips.

figma.name: Lemon granite morning
figma.note: Gunmetal gray + blue with a bright yellow accent — named for financial services.

figma.name: Neutral elegance
figma.note: Beige + gray + brown, 'serene and professional' — no hue is strong enough to be mistaken for a status colour.

figma.name: Frozen mist
figma.note: Warm monochromatic gray with cinnamon — 'great for CTA buttons and clickable elements urging action'.

figma.name: Amethyst dawn haze
figma.note: Soft purple ground with vibrant yellow as the complement — 'draws the eye to buttons or calls to action'.

figma.name: Sandstone aquamarine serenity
figma.note: Earth ground + pastel blue accent, to be used 'sparingly for buttons, links, or highlighted text'.

figma.name: Emerald lavender lake
figma.note: Low-chroma green/blue/lilac triad — nothing here can be misread as a semantic status colour.

figma.name: Driftwood pearl morning
figma.note: Rose gold + brown + blue on light gray — 'a neutral background that enhances readability'.
